bullets: Which of the four red curves fits the data (blue dots) best?
Which curve is expected to generalize the best?
Are they both the same? If yes, why? If no, why not?
Lesson: Simple models should be preferred over complicated models
Too simple a model can underfit (e.g., M = 0 above)
General guideline: Choose a model not-too-simple, yet not-too-complex

visual_elements.description: 2x2 grid of four small polynomial curve-fitting plots. Each shows blue scatter dots (data points), a green sinusoidal true curve, and a red fitted curve. Top-left labeled 'M = 0': red curve is a flat horizontal line (underfit). Top-right labeled 'M = 1': red curve is a straight sloped line. Bottom-left labeled 'M = 3': red curve is a smooth cubic closely following the green curve. Bottom-right labeled 'M = 9': red curve is a highly wiggly high-degree polynomial passing through every blue dot (overfit). Axes have small tick marks but no readable numeric labels.
